description: Hoosier Resilience Index is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Environmental Resilience Institute. Communities in Indiana can check this statewide map to explore information on extreme heat, extreme precipitation, and floodplain land use data. The map shows current trends and 2050 emission scenarios for extreme heat and precipitation events, based on the Indiana Climate Change Impacts Assessment. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Extreme Heat, Flooding – General. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Natural Areas and Wildlife, People, Urban Landscape and Tree Canopy. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
